transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... things have just been really difficult lately. Since my in-laws moved into our house, I've been so keyed up and just completely worn down. It's affecting everything. I find myself snapping at my wife all the time, which isn't like me. And at work—I'm an agent for artists and musicians—I'm avoiding calls I would normally handle immediately. It got so bad that I nearly let a major musician's contract fall apart just because I couldn't think straight. I just feel like I'm losing my grip on things.
When exactly did these feelings of being keyed up and worn down start—was it right around the time your in-laws moved in, or had you been feeling this way before that?

No, I was functioning completely normally before they moved in. It really just... it all started within a few weeks of them taking over the house. Before that, I wasn't having any of these issues at all.
When your in-laws moved in, did you experience any moment where you felt intense fear, horror, or a sense that you or someone else was in serious danger?

No, nothing like that. It wasn't... I wasn't scared for my life or anything. It's just been this constant, overwhelming stress since they got here, but no, no intense fear or feeling like we were in danger. Just... really, really stressed.
Do you think your in-laws will eventually move out, or do you expect them to stay in your house permanently?

Well, they're still living with us right now. The whole arrangement hasn't ended. So... all these issues I'm dealing with are happening right in the middle of it, while they are still in the house. It's very much an active situation. I certainly hope it's not permanent, but they haven't moved out, and there's no clear end date in sight.

Since your in-laws moved in a few weeks ago, have you had any periods where you felt even slightly better or back to normal, or has it been this constant feeling of being keyed up and worn down every single day without any relief?

No, there really hasn't been any break from it. It's just... it's been constant. Every single day since they got here, I wake up feeling just as wound up and exhausted as the day before. I haven't had a single day where I felt like myself or even just a little bit relaxed. It's just relentless.

If your in-laws were to move out tomorrow, do you think these feelings of being keyed up and worn down would go away fairly quickly, or do you think they might continue even after the stressor is gone?

I don't really know for sure. I mean... I'd like to think that if they just packed up and left tomorrow, I'd feel better. But honestly, I'm so worn down right now, I'm not sure if it would just switch off instantly. I guess I haven't really thought about it because there's no sign of them leaving anytime soon.

Let me ask you this differently—have you noticed that your anxiety or stress symptoms get noticeably worse when you're actually around your in-laws, or are they pretty much the same level whether they're home, at work, or anywhere else?

Well, honestly, it's pretty much the same level all the time. I mean, sure, if they're right in front of me, it's stressful, but even when they're out of the house running errands or whatever, I'm still just as keyed up. It's like I'm just waiting for them to come back, so the feeling doesn't really go away just because they aren't in the room.

You mentioned that even when your in-laws aren't home, you still feel keyed up. But let me ask more specifically: if this living situation were to completely resolve—say they moved out and stayed out—do you think these symptoms would gradually fade away over time, or do you worry they might stick around even after the stressor is gone?

Well, it's hard to predict because... they're still living with us. The arrangement hasn't ended yet. So all these issues I'm having are happening right now, while the situation is still completely active. It's not like they moved out months ago and I'm still feeling this way. 

I would hope that if they actually left for good, these feelings would gradually fade away... but since they are still very much in my house and there's no end in sight, I just don't know for sure how I'll feel when it's actually over.

When you imagine your in-laws actually moving out and the situation being completely resolved, do you feel confident that your anxiety and stress would gradually go away, or do you have a worry in the back of your mind that these feelings might linger on even after they're gone?

Honestly, like I was just saying, it's hard to be confident either way because... well, the living arrangement hasn't ended yet. All of this stress is happening right now while the situation with them is still completely active. It's not like they moved out six months ago, the problem was resolved, and I'm still sitting here feeling like this. We're just still right in the middle of it, so I really don't know how I'll feel once they're actually gone.
If your in-laws moved out tomorrow and stayed out, how long do you think it would take before you felt back to normal—a few days, a couple of weeks, or longer than that?

I mean, I really couldn't give you an exact timeline. Like I mentioned before, the living arrangement still hasn't ended. They're still in my house. So all this stress and anxiety, it's happening right now while the situation is completely active. It's not like they moved out months ago and the problem was resolved and I'm still dealing with this. Since we're still right in the thick of it, I just don't know how long it would take to feel normal again.

Let me ask you this clearly: if your in-laws moved out tomorrow and the living situation ended completely, do you believe your symptoms would go away, or do you think they might continue even after that stressor is completely removed?

I'm really not sure how else to answer that, doctor. I feel like I'm just repeating myself at this point. The living arrangement hasn't ended. These problems I'm having are happening right now because the in-law situation is still completely active. It's not like the issue was resolved months ago and I'm still sitting here feeling like this. Since they are still in my house, I just can't give you a clear yes or no on what will happen after they eventually leave.

I understand the situation is still ongoing. But setting that aside for a moment—based on how you're feeling right now, if your in-laws moved out and stayed gone, do you think these feelings of being keyed up and worn down would completely go away once the stressor is removed?

Look, I... I know you're trying to get a specific answer from me, but I really can't give you one. I don't know how else to say it. The living arrangement hasn't ended. They are still living in my house. These problems, the stress, being so worn down... it's all happening right now because the situation is still completely active. It's not like they moved out months ago, everything was resolved, and I'm just lingering on it. They're still there. So I really don't know what will happen or how I'll feel when they finally do leave.

I understand they're still living with you. But let me ask you this: do you think the core reason you're feeling this way—being keyed up and worn down—is specifically because of having your in-laws in your house, or could there be something else going on with you that's separate from that situation?

No, I really believe it's specifically because of them. I mean, I'm here talking to you because ever since my in-laws moved into our house, I've just been so keyed up and worn down. There isn't anything else going on. 

It's just that situation, and it's bleeding into everything else. I'm constantly snapping at my wife now. And work... well, work is suffering. I'm avoiding calls I would normally handle immediately, and I actually nearly let a musician's contract fall apart recently just because I couldn't think straight. None of this was happening before they moved in.

Since your in-laws moved in a few weeks ago, have you noticed any change in how you're feeling—like is the stress and being keyed up getting worse over time, staying exactly the same, or actually getting a little bit better as you adjust?

Honestly, it's... it's just staying exactly the same. It hasn't gotten any better, but I wouldn't say it's getting worse either. It's just a constant, steady level of being completely worn out and stressed every single day since they got here.

I know the situation is still active, but I want to understand something important: if your in-laws moved out tomorrow, do you think your symptoms would go away completely once they're gone, or would they likely continue and persist even after that stressor is removed?

I... I know we just went over this a minute ago, but I really just don't have an answer for you. I honestly don't know. If they packed up and left tomorrow, maybe I'd feel better right away, or maybe it would take a while to unwind from all this. I just can't say for sure what's going to happen after they're actually gone.

I want to ask you something a bit different. Over the past few weeks since your in-laws moved in, have you noticed your worry or anxiety expanding to other areas of your life beyond just the in-law situation—like worrying about money, your health, your job performance, or other things that aren't directly related to them being in your house?

No, not really. I mean, I know I mentioned work is taking a hit, but I'm not actually sitting around worrying about my career or money or my health or anything like that. It's not like that. All my stress is just... it's entirely focused on them being in my house and what's happening there. I haven't really found myself getting anxious about those other areas you mentioned.

When you imagine a realistic scenario where your in-laws eventually move out—not today, but at some point in the future—do you expect that once they're gone and the situation is truly over, your anxiety and stress would gradually fade away back to how you were before they arrived?

I mean... I guess I'd expect things to go back to normal eventually. But they're still here right now. The situation is still very much ongoing. It's not like they left months ago and I'm still feeling this way... they're literally in my house right now, so that's why I'm dealing with all this stress. It's happening while they're here.

When you say you'd expect things to go back to normal eventually once your in-laws move out, do you actually believe your symptoms would fully go away and you'd return to how you were before they arrived, or do you have a sense that you might be left dealing with these feelings even after they're gone?

I mean, honestly, I really don't know for sure. I'd like to think that once they're out of the house, I'd go back to being myself, but... I just don't know. It's hard to predict how I'll feel when it actually happens. Right now, I'm just so deep in it, I can't really tell you if it'll all just vanish the second they walk out the door.

You've mentioned you'd like to think things would go back to normal once they leave, but you're not sure. Let me ask you directly: if your in-laws moved out and stayed gone permanently, do you genuinely expect your anxiety and stress would completely resolve and you'd feel like yourself again, or do you suspect these feelings might stick around even after they're no longer in your house?

I really just... I don't know. I mean, if they were gone permanently, I'd hope I would just go back to normal. But I can't say for sure. I'm just so overwhelmed with them being here right now that I can't really picture what it's going to be like after. I just don't have a clear answer for you on that.

If your in-laws moved out tomorrow and the situation was completely resolved, would you expect these feelings of being keyed up and worn down to go away, or are you worried they might stick around even after they're gone?

Look, I really can't give you a better answer than what I just said. If they left tomorrow... I honestly don't know if I'd bounce right back or if this... this feeling would just stay with me. I'm just so worn down right now, I can't even imagine them not being here, let alone how I'd feel after. I just don't know.
